title: Search In Rotated Sorted Array
description: A sorted array of **unique** integers was rotated an unknown number of times. Given the rotated array `nums` and an integer `target`, return the index of `target`, or `-1` if it is not present. Your algorithm must run in O(log n) time.
hints: Plain binary search fails because the array is not globally sorted. But after splitting at mid, is some part always sorted?
At each step either [left, mid] or [mid, right] is sorted. You can test that by comparing nums[left] with nums[mid].
Once you know the sorted half, check whether target falls inside its range; keep that half if so, otherwise discard it and search the other.

solution.explanation: At every step one of the two halves around mid is sorted: if nums[left] <= nums[mid] the left half is, otherwise the right half is. If the target lies within the sorted half's bounds, search that half; otherwise search the other. Each step halves the range, giving O(log n) time and O(1) space.
